rationale: The review is a pure pricing/business-model complaint about DLC strategy, not a bug or technical issue. The case notes correctly identify this as non-actionable subjective feedback requiring no_action. The retrieved chunks contain information about free content (Skills 2.0 update, First World Bank free DLC, free-play-when-invited mechanics) that an ideal responder could cite to acknowledge the game's free-content offerings, but the gold answer does not require these chunks — it requires only that the responder recognize the complaint as design feedback outside the scope of bug triage and take no action. The absence of DLC-pricing-justification material is appropriate; an ideal responder would not argue DLC value (per case notes) and would simply decline to engage. The pool's presence of free-content information does not contradict the no_action posture.
